text: - cyte or granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating fac- tor.1,2,5 Infection is a major cause of morbidity and mortal- ity after transplantation, so prophylactic cover with antimicrobials2,21,22 and normal immunoglobulins is rec- ommended,21 although the value of the latter has been questioned.23 Granulocyte colony-stimulating factors are sometimes used after allogeneic transplants to hasten hae- matopoietic recovery. While a meta-analysis found no ev- idence for an increase in risk for acute or chronic graft- versus-host disease,24 a large study found delayed platelet engraftment, increased graft-versus-host disease, and in- creased mortality in those given growth factors after allo- geneic bone marrow transplants; these effects were not seen in patients given allogeneic PBSCT.25 In addition to such supportive care, patients who have re- ceived allogeneic transplants require immunosuppressive therapy aimed at the prevention of graft-versus-host dis- ease (GVHD). GVHD is usually characterised as acute or chronic depending on the manifestations, and the time of presentation1,4,5,10,26-28 (by convention acute disease oc- curs within a hundred days of transplantation, and chronic disease after this time, although in practice there is consid- erable overlap). The organ systems primarily affected are skin, liver, lung, and gastrointestinal tract. Both forms are marked by mac- ulopapular rashes, which in severe disease may progress to bullous lesions and epidermal necrolysis. Liver disease may include cholestatic jaundice (usually in the acute form) and hepatitis; symptoms may need to be distin- guished from the veno-occlusive disease (VOD) which sometimes complicates bone marrow transplantation and is due to the pre-transplant conditioning regimen (VOD may respond to treatment with antithrombin III29 or defibrotide30,31). Ursodeoxycholic acid has been found to be of benefit for the prophylaxis of hepatic complica- tions.32 The main symptom of gastrointestinal GVHD is diarrhoea, often severe and painful. In patients with chron- ic GVHD other manifestations may include arthritis, mu- cositis, lung disease, and scleroderma. Most modern regimens for the prophylaxis of GVHD after allogeneic HSCT are based on ciclosporin. Although GVHD still occurs in many ciclosporin-treated patients, morbidity is much reduced and survival improved. Com- bination regimens have been tried for prophylaxis, partic- ularly ciclosporin or tacrolimus with methotrexate, but also combinations with other drugs including antilym- phocyte immunoglobulins, corticosteroids, mycopheno- late mofetil, and sirolimus.9,19,33 Monoclo
